terms.definition: An open-source operating system kernel combined with GNU tools to form a complete OS
terms.example: Amazon Linux, Ubuntu, and CentOS are all Linux distributions

terms.definition: A proprietary multi-user operating system developed in the 1960s that inspired Linux
terms.example: Unix required expensive licensing fees, which motivated the creation of free Linux

terms.definition: The core component of an operating system that directly manages hardware resources
terms.example: The Linux kernel handles CPU scheduling, memory allocation, and device drivers

terms.definition: A command interpreter that accepts user commands and translates them into kernel actions
terms.example: Bash is the most common shell in Linux, where you type commands like ls and cd

terms.definition: GNU's Not Unix - a project that created free Unix-like utilities and tools
terms.example: GNU tools like bash, ls, and cp combined with Linux kernel create a complete OS

terms.definition: The top-level directory in Linux file system from which all other directories branch
terms.example: All paths in Linux start from / like /home/ec2-user or /var/log

terms.definition: The administrator account in Linux with complete control over the system
terms.example: Root user's prompt shows # symbol and home directory is /root

terms.definition: A user's personal directory for storing their files and settings
terms.example: For ec2-user, ~ represents /home/ec2-user; for root, ~ represents /root

terms.definition: Text-based interface where users type commands instead of clicking graphical elements
terms.example: In Linux CLI, you type cd /home to navigate instead of clicking folders

terms.definition: Visual interface with windows, icons, and mouse interactions
terms.example: Windows desktop with folders you can click is a GUI; Linux servers typically use CLI

terms.definition: A complete operating system built around Linux kernel with specific tools and configurations
terms.example: Amazon Linux, Ubuntu, and Kali are different Linux distributions for different purposes

terms.definition: Software that installs, updates, and manages programs from repositories
terms.example: yum for Amazon Linux/CentOS, apt for Ubuntu - use 'yum install nginx' to install software

terms.definition: Treatment of uppercase and lowercase letters as distinct characters
terms.example: In Linux, File.txt and file.txt are completely different files

terms.definition: Complete path from root directory (/) to a file or directory
terms.example: /home/ec2-user/documents/file.txt is an absolute path starting from /

terms.definition: Path relative to current directory, not starting from root
terms.example: If in /home/ec2-user, typing cd documents uses relative path

terms.definition: Collections of pre-written code that programs use to perform common tasks
terms.example: glibc provides functions like printf() that programs call instead of writing from scratch

terms.definition: Software whose source code is freely available for anyone to view, modify, and distribute
terms.example: Linux source code is publicly available on kernel.org for anyone to download and modify

terms.definition: AWS browser-based SSH client for connecting to Linux EC2 instances
terms.example: Click Connect button in EC2 console to access your Linux instance without external SSH client

terms.definition: Regular user account with limited privileges, cannot modify system files
terms.example: ec2-user is a standard user, shown by $ in prompt, can't access /root directory

terms.definition: Command that displays the absolute path of your current location
terms.example: Type pwd to see where you are, output might be /home/ec2-user

terms.definition: File system that doesn't store real files on disk but provides interface to kernel data
terms.example: /proc and /sys are virtual - files show live system info but don't actually exist on disk
